site.name: Boltget
site.description: A download manager built for speed. Splits every file across many connections and picks up where it stopped, even after a crash.

footer.tagline: The download manager built for speed.

home.title: Boltget: every byte, at full speed
home.description: A download manager built for speed. Splits every file across many connections and picks up where it stopped, even after a crash.
home.lede: Boltget splits every file across many connections, keeps each one busy to the last byte, and never loses its place.

app.label: A demonstration of the Boltget app, simulated in the page. Pick a file with the buttons above it to watch it download: a new row appears, the file map fills from several connections at once and the download finishes.
app.caption: A simulation of the app, sped up.

speed.heading: Many connections. One file.
speed.lede: Boltget [reads the server first], splits the file into parts and adds connections [only while they make it faster]. When one finishes early, it [takes over] the biggest part left.

card.label: A simulated download shown as a map of squares, one per slice of the file. Connections fill their own parts at the same time until the whole file has arrived.
card.legend: Each square is a slice of the file.

probe.body: One request learns the file's size and whether the server can send it in parts.

split.body: Connections start on parts of their own, and more join only while the download gets faster.

steal.body: A connection that runs out of work takes half of the biggest part left, so they all finish together.

resume.heading: Pull the plug. It picks up where it stopped.
resume.lede: Progress counts only once the bytes are [safely on disk]. After a crash, a restart or a dropped line, the download [carries on from there], not from zero.

card.label: A download in the Boltget app is interrupted by a power cut, shows as paused, then resumes from where it stopped and finishes.

builtin.heading: The details, handled.
builtin.lede: The things a download manager should simply do, [with nothing to set up] and [nothing to babysit].

queues.body: Line downloads up and let a few run at a time while the rest wait their turn.

limits.body: For one download or all of them, changed while they run.

refresh.body: Link expired near the end? Give it a new one and it carries on.

proxy.body: HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5, with cookies and sign-in when a site needs them.

cli.body: Every download from a terminal, with exit codes and JSON for scripts.

verified.body: Checksums are computed on the way in, so a damaged file never passes as done.

builtin.next: Coming next: browser extension and video downloads.

cta.heading: Faster from the first byte.
cta.lede: Install it, paste a link, and watch the file arrive.
cta.mark: The Boltget mark lighting up row by row.

bench.title: Benchmarks
bench.description: Median download times for Boltget and another download manager at default settings, with the method and the raw data.
bench.heading: Measured, not promised.
bench.lede: The same files, downloaded again and again by Boltget and [another download manager], both at their defaults. Lower is faster.
bench.chartLabel: Median download time per test, in seconds, for Boltget and another download manager. Each pair of bars is scaled to its own test.

result.faster: Boltget was faster in every run on {count} of {total} tests.
result.slower: The other download manager was faster in every run on {count} of {total}.
result.overlap: Where the runs overlap, we claim no difference.

targets.lab-throttled-100mib: 100 MiB from a server that slows each connection
